app_info.subtitle: Deploy and manage cloud apps
app_info.description: Lizard is a cloud platform for deploying and managing containerized apps and managed databases. Ask it to deploy a GitHub repo, provision a Postgres, Redis, or S3 addon, check logs and metrics, manage secrets, scale services, or attach a custom domain — all scoped to your own Lizard workspaces and projects.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads the caller's own identity from the auth token; no writes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Calls Lizard's own /api/auth/me endpoint, nothing external.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read, no state change possible.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the caller's workspaces, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the caller's projects, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new project record.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only within Lizard's own platform API.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new project; never overwrites or removes an existing one, even if called again with the same name.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists available deployment regions, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists apps/addons in a project, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one service's config/status, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new app or addon, optionally triggering a build/deploy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Any GitHub repo it builds from is fetched through Lizard's own build pipeline, not an open-ended action the tool takes on its own.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new service; calling it again, even with the same name, creates another one rather than overwriting or removing anything existing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Provisions a new managed addon (Postgres/Redis/S3).
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only within Lizard's own platform API.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new addon; never overwrites or removes an existing one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes a new service name.
justifications.destructive_justification: A name change is fully reversible (renaming back restores the prior state) and touches no data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes the service and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes replica count / CPU / memory / storage limits.
justifications.destructive_justification: Resource limits and replica count can be freely raised or lowered again; no data is removed (storage is grow-only, a safety constraint, not a destructive action).

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the configured container port, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes the container port.
justifications.destructive_justification: A config value change, fully reversible by setting it back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes build/deploy config fields (repo, branch, build/start commands, etc.).
justifications.destructive_justification: Every field it touches is an editable config value, reversible by setting it again; it does not delete the service or any data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Triggers a new build and deploy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Builds run through Lizard's own build pipeline against the already-configured repo.
justifications.destructive_justification: Redeploying existing source doesn't remove anything; a failed build simply doesn't replace the running version.

justifications.read_only_justification: Restarts the running service.
justifications.destructive_justification: A restart with no rebuild causes no data loss.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads deploy/build history and pod status, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a bounded snapshot of recent log output, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads CPU/memory/network metrics, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a cost/usage summary, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists secret keys (values masked unless reveal:true), no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes one or more secret values, overwriting any existing value at the same key.
justifications.destructive_justification: Overwriting a key is a normal, reversible config write (setting it again restores prior behavior); it doesn't delete the service, remove other secrets, or cause irreversible data loss the way service_delete/secrets_delete do.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes one or more secrets.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes the secret values and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists available ${{addon.KEY}} reference templates, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Attaches a custom domain or generates a new *.onlizard.com subdomain.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always adds a domain; it never removes an existing one (calling it again without a hostname just generates another subdomain, per its description).

justifications.read_only_justification: Performs a real DNS check against the hostname and updates that domain's verification status server-side; it's not a pure read of already-stored state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Verifying a domain doesn't remove or alter any other data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a custom domain from a service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes the domain and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Switches the tracked branch and triggers a redeploy.
justifications.destructive_justification: Switching branches and redeploying doesn't delete anything; prior build history and the previous branch setting are both still recoverable.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads GitHub connection status and tracked repo/branch per service, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only returns an install URL string; it does not perform the GitHub connection itself. The actual connection only happens if the user opens that URL in a browser and approves it, so calling this tool alone changes no state.
justifications.destructive_justification: No state change results from calling it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a shell command inside the service's container.
justifications.open_world_justification: This is the one tool that leaves Lizard's own bounded API: it executes an arbitrary, caller-supplied shell command inside the user's own running container, so its effects and outputs are open-ended and unpredictable, not limited to a fixed set of platform operations.
justifications.destructive_justification: An arbitrary shell command can delete files or otherwise cause irreversible changes inside the container; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Applies a bulk, config-as-code style update to services/addons/secrets in one request.
justifications.destructive_justification: The config body is passed through verbatim and can overwrite or remove existing fields in one call, per its own description; marked destructive to reflect that a single call can silently replace or drop existing configuration, unlike the narrower single-field tools.

test_cases.description: Deploy a public GitHub repo as a new service in a specific region
test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy https://github.com/lizard-build/codex-react-test to Lizard in the EU West Limburg region
test_cases.expected_output: Confirms a new service was created and a build was triggered for the given repo/region. Does not report a domain immediately — states the domain isn't assigned until the build finishes and offers to check back.

test_cases.description: Check recent logs for a running service
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the last logs from my api service
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a bounded snapshot of recent log lines from the matched service, not a live stream.

test_cases.description: Provision a Postgres addon and wire it into an existing app via a secret reference
test_cases.user_prompt: Add a Postgres database to my project and connect it to my api service
test_cases.expected_output: Creates a Postgres addon, then sets a secret on the app referencing the addon's connection string via ${{name.KEY}} rather than printing raw credentials, and tells the user which ${{name.KEY}} refs are available.

test_cases.description: Scale a service's replica count and memory
test_cases.user_prompt: Scale my worker service to 3 replicas and 1GB of memory
test_cases.expected_output: Confirms the replica count and memory limit were both updated on the matched service.

test_cases.description: Ambiguous service name across multiple projects — edge case requiring disambiguation
test_cases.expected_output: If more than one project has a service named 'api', asks the user which project before calling deploy_restart, rather than guessing one.

negative_test_cases.description: General knowledge question unrelated to any Lizard account or service
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's the weather like in Berlin today?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Answers directly without calling any Lizard tool — the question has nothing to do with the user's Lizard resources.

negative_test_cases.description: Generic coding help with no connection to the user's Lizard account
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write me a Python function that reverses a string
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Writes the function directly without calling any Lizard tool — no service, deploy, or account action is implied.

negative_test_cases.description: Request to act outside Lizard's actual capability — an arbitrary machine, not a Lizard-hosted service container
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: SSH into my personal laptop at 192.168.1.50 and delete some files
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Declines — ssh_exec only runs commands inside the user's own Lizard service containers, not arbitrary external machines, and does not attempt the request.
